description:
Case 9, plan view: A signalized intersection (circled S at the center) of a main street running left to right and a cross street running up and down. Both approaches on the main street have a hatched raised island or median in the lane next to the curb side of the roadway, shown as a long rectangle with rounded ends, with a vehicle in the adjacent lane. On the left approach the hatched strip is dimensioned '<20'' for its width. Each approach strip is labeled R13A(CA) with a post symbol and R9-3'S, and a small hatched half-round island at the intersection end of each strip is labeled R13A with a leader to a short line at the stop location marked 'NOTE 11'. Inside the intersection the pavement text KEEP CLEAR is drawn (mirrored on the scan) across the crossing street's box. A sign callout R10-6 over R13A(CA) is placed at the upper left corner curb return. Below the hatched strip the main street shows dashed white lane lines ending in solid stop lines at the crosswalk and a double yellow curved left-turn lane line with a left-turn arrow. The right approach repeats the same pattern as a mirror image.

Case 10, plan view: The same intersection with a single hatched island on the left approach drawn as a tapered nose that ends in two chevron markings and diagonal lines pointing toward the intersection, with a left pointing arrow above it. Dashed lane lines, a left-turn arrow and a double yellow lane line are shown as in Case 9. On the right approach a hatched island has a vehicle crossing the stop line at an angle, with an R1-1 stop sign on a post, a dimension '20' MIN.' measured from the cross street curb line to the sign location and a left pointing arrow labeled 'NOTE 12' next to a diagonal leader line.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Location of Limit Lines and Crosswalks, Drawing No. S-493.0, sheet 5 of 7.
notes: No numbered notes are printed on this sheet. Callouts and legends on the sheet: 1. KEEP CLEAR pavement legend in the intersection (Case 9). 2. R10-6 and R13A(CA) signs at the upper left curb return (Case 9). 3. R13A(CA) and R9-3S signs at each hatched strip (Case 9). 4. R13A sign at the hatched half-round island, see Note 11 (Case 9). 5. Hatched strip width less than 20 ft (<20') (Case 9). 6. R1-1 stop sign with a 20 ft minimum (20' MIN.) dimension, see Note 12 (Case 10). Notes 11 and 12 are referenced but are not printed on this sheet and appear on another sheet of the set.
title: Location of Limit Lines and Crosswalks (Cases 9 and 10)
summary: Two plan cases showing where to place limit lines, keep clear areas and signs at a signalized intersection (circled S) where a hatched island meets the approach. Case 9 shows hatched islands under 20 ft wide with R13A(CA), R9-3S, R13A and R10-6 signs and a KEEP CLEAR legend in the intersection. Case 10 shows a hatched island nose with chevrons and an R1-1 stop sign with a 20 ft minimum dimension. The notes cited (Notes 11 and 12) are not printed on this sheet.

description:
Case 11, plan view: A two-way street with a hatched median or island on the upper side. A vehicle on the left side of the island stops at an R1-1 stop sign on a post at the island end, with a 5' MIN. dimension from the stop sign to the end of the island. A second vehicle on the right is on a curved dashed path leaving the opposite side, and a symmetric R1-1 stop sign and 5' MIN. dimension appear at the right island end. Dashed lane lines with solid stop line ends and a double line are shown below.

Case 12, plan view: A similar street layout with a left pointing arrow. On the left a hatched median ends in a nose with chevron markings and a sign labeled W12-1 below it. On the right an R6-1 sign and an R1-1 stop sign (with vehicle and left pointing arrow) are shown. Curved dashed vehicle paths cross the street between the left and right sides. A hatched double yellow center median runs the full length with dashed lane lines on both sides.

Case 13, plan view: A signalized (circled S) crosswalk drawn with transverse black bars across a multilane street. Stop lines are set back 5' (dimension arrows marked 5') on both sides of the crosswalk, with a label 'NOTE 13 & 15' on the right side. A solid line turns the corner left of the crosswalk, separating a double yellow turn lane. Dashed lane lines continue on both sides.

Case 14, plan view: The same crosswalk with a 5' dimension to the stop line on both sides. The left approach has a 12" YELLOW line drawn diagonally across the center lane and the pavement legends WAIT HERE (mirrored and rotated on the scan) in each lane next to the crosswalk side, with a driveway symbol (box with an X) at the curb. Label 'NOTES 13, 14 & 15'. The right approach shows a driveway symbol at the curb.

Case 15, plan view: The same crosswalk with 5' dimensions. The left approach has WAIT HERE legends in two lanes next to a stop line and a driveway symbol at the curb. The right approach has a driveway at the curb about 5' from the crosswalk and a '2' WHITE OR YELLOW' line labeled at the crosswalk edge, with label 'NOTE 15'.

description:
Case 1: Stop sign control, plan view: A skewed signalized intersection (circled S) with the main street running left to right and the cross street running diagonally. The lane lines, dashed lane dividers and turn arrows are drawn on all legs. In the lower right quadrant a triangular channelizing island forms a channelized right turn with a curved right-turn roadway, with a 'Radius' dimension line labeled on the curb return. To the right of the plan is the R1-1 STOP sign graphic (red octagon with white STOP legend), labeled R1-1.

Case 2: Yield sign control, plan view: A square intersection (circled S) with a signalized center box, left turn pockets with arrows on each leg, and dashed lane lines. In the lower right quadrant a triangular island with striped crosswalk bars across the right-turn roadway is labeled R1-2 and a 'Radius' dimension is shown on the curb return arc. A callout reads '2' white or yellow, 5' C-C' for the crosswalk bars. To the right of the plan is the R1-2 YIELD sign graphic (red and white inverted triangle) labeled R1-2.

Title block: Approved February 13, 2006, for Frances T. Banerjee, Interim General Manager. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Channelized Right Turns, sheet 1 of 5, Drawing No. S-494.0. Drawn by MT. Principal traffic engineer entry 88.
notes:
CASE 1: STOP SIGN CONTROL. Note: Use Stop sign operation where the curb return radius is less than 20 feet (10 miles per hour design speed), pedestrian traffic across the channelized right turn is high, cross-traffic visibility is restricted, or where the use of a Yield sign has been shown to be inadequate.

CASE 2: YIELD SIGN CONTROL. Note: Use Yield sign operation where the curb return radius is 20 feet (10 miles per hour design speed) or greater and pedestrian traffic across the channelized right turn is low.

Callouts: R1-1 (stop sign), R1-2 (yield sign), 2' white or yellow, 5' center to center (C-C), Radius.
title: Channelized Right Turns
summary: First sheet of five on channelized right turns. It gives the criteria for the two simplest controls and shows an intersection plan for each. Case 1 uses an R1-1 stop sign where the curb return radius is under 20 ft, pedestrian traffic is high, cross-traffic visibility is restricted or a yield sign has proved inadequate. Case 2 uses an R1-2 yield sign where the radius is 20 ft or more and pedestrian traffic is low. Approved February 13, 2006. The merge, added lane cases and tables are on later sheets.

NOTES:
1. Bike lane symbols are recommended to clarify the intended operation of the bike lane space.
2. Optional use of green colored pavement to enhance visibility and conspicuity of bicycle lane. Green colored pavement may be installed for the entire length of the bicycle lane or for only a portion (or portions) of the bicycle lane. All green colored pavement should comply with FHWA Interim Approval for Optional Use of Green Colored Pavement for Bike Lanes (IA-14) and approved by LADOT.

Title block: Approved 11-09-2022, for Connie Llanos, Interim General Manager. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Neighborhood Watch Signs, sheet 1 of 1, Dwg. No. S-508.0. Checked by Priv. Engr., Sr. T.E. TF, Pr. T.E. BG, drawn by Priv Engr, T.E. SR.
notes:
Authority: Installation of these signs is subject to completion of an "Application for Installation of Official Neighborhood Watch Sign" and receipt of Los Angeles Department of Transportation (LADOT) approval. The name of elected officials, donating parties, sponsoring parties, neighborhood groups or neighborhood councils, etc. shall not be shown on the sign.

Sign: Size shall be no greater than 24 inches vertically and 18 inches horizontally. Appearance should be similar to one of the two samples on the right. Colors should be reflectorized. Trademarked logos shall not be used without permission from the owner. Anti-graffiti film should be used. Material shall be 0.08 inch minimum thickness aluminum stock, pre-drilled with two 3/8 inch diameter holes, centered with one near the top of the sign and one near the bottom. Corners of sign shall have a minimum 0.50 inch radius.

Installation: Signs shall be manufactured and installed only by qualified sign companies approved by LADOT. Signs should be installed on non-wooden street lighting poles. They may be installed on street lighting poles with parking restriction signs. However, they may not be installed on traffic signal poles, nor on street lighting poles with other warning, regulatory, or guidance traffic signs facing the same direction. If existing poles or posts are not available, signs may be installed on new posts (see LADOT DWG. No. S-452). They shall be installed at a clearance height greater than 7 feet. LADOT reserves the right to remove Neighborhood Watch Signs not in conformance with these guidelines.

Maintenance: LADOT is not responsible for the maintenance of these signs. If the signs are damaged or stolen, the local group is responsible for sign replacement and reinstallation.
title: Neighborhood Watch Signs
summary: Rules for installing and maintaining official Neighborhood Watch signs, with two sample sign layouts. Installation needs an application and LADOT approval, and no names of officials, sponsors or groups may appear. Signs go on non-wooden street lighting poles at a clearance above 7 ft, are no larger than 24 inches by 18 inches, and are replaced by the local group. Aluminum material is 0.08 inch minimum with two 3/8 inch holes and 0.50 inch minimum corner radius.

description:

The bus bulb is a raised floating island along the curb with a rounded nose at the left end carrying an R9-6 and OM1-1 sign post. The bulb length is marked 'BUS BULB LENGTH SEE NOTE 6' and its width is 8' MIN (see Notes 5, 10 and 11), with the end of the bulb 10' from the crosswalk. Next to the bulb a Class IV bike lane (shaded, with an arrow and bicycle lane symbol) passes behind it, and 12" white or yellow crosswalk bars with bicycle yield line triangles (typ) cross the bike lane at both ends, with green colored surface recommended (see Note 2). The bulb includes a 5' x 8' MIN. forward boarding and alighting area (see Note 5) near the right end, a potential bus shelter location (see Note 3), a 12' x 4' or 5' x 8' MIN. clear zone for the rear boarding and alighting area (see Note 8), and a red curb along the street side. The existing sidewalk is 5' MIN. width (see Note 7).

Sign details: R9-6 (bicycle YIELD TO PEDS) and OM1-1 (object marker with nine circles).

Type II floating bus bulb, intermediate elevation, bike lane (plan view, lower): The same layout with a bicycle ramp at each end of the bulb. Each ramp is marked with a Chevron IV bicycle ramp marking (typ) and labeled 'BICYCLE RAMP 12.5% MAX. SLOPE', and the bike lane has 12" white or yellow crosswalk bars and yellow yield lines. The same labels apply: 24" white or yellow crosswalk, 10' from crosswalk, 8' MIN (see Notes 5, 10 and 11), bus bulb length (see Note 6), 12' x 4' or 5' x 8' MIN clear zone for rear boarding and alighting area (see Note 8), potential bus shelter location (see Note 3), red curb, Class IV bike lane, 5' MIN width existing sidewalk (see Note 7).

Shelter and railing placement guidance (section): A cross section from the bus bulb at the left to the sidewalk at the right. The bus shelter stands on the bulb with an accessible route of 4' MIN, 5' PREF measured from the bulb curb to the shelter. The shelter roof overhangs 24" MIN beyond the bulb curb. A pedestrian handrail (see Notes 1 and 12 and S-463) stands 18" from the shelter and at least 10" from the curb of the sloped bike lane between the bulb and the sidewalk.

description:
Mini-roundabouts, plan view: A four-leg intersection with a circular center island (labeled CENTER ISLAND MOUNTABLE OR PAINTED, see Note 1 and sheet 2) in the middle, surrounded by a dashed circulating path. Each approach has a tapered mountable splitter island in the middle of the street (the left and right legs show them as single tapers and the top and bottom legs show them as two pieces separated by the crosswalk), marked with solid white edge lines and 4" solid yellow edge lines 1' off the mountable center and splitter islands. A dashed white entrance line (12" wide, 2' long at a 2' gap) marks the entry to each approach, with solid white arrow symbols on the pavement (optional for raised islands, required for painted islands). Crosswalks of transverse bars are placed 20' (TYP) back from the circulating roadway, see Note 6. Corner curb returns have non-walkable area strips along the curb. On the right approach an optional splitter island is formed by two sets of double yellow lines (see Note 1 on sheet 2). At the lower right corner an optional red curb is marked (see DOT Std Plan S-481).

Sign layout (shown for one approach): R1-2 YIELD sign with R6-5P (roundabout circular arrows plaque), W11-2 pedestrian sign with W16-7PL (arrow plaque) or Assembly "B" (CA), W11-2 or Assembly "D" (CA), W2-6 roundabout warning sign (optional) with W16-8 (street name plaque, 7TH AVE.) or W16-17P (ROUNDABOUT plaque) (both optional). Pavement legends PED XING and a YIELD legend with yield triangles (optional) are on the lower approach. Vertical dimension lines on the lower approach read 100', 200' and 32', running beside the sign posts and the XING and PED pavement legends.

Title block: Approved 02-20-2020, for Seleta Reynolds, General Manager. City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Mini-Roundabouts and Neighborhood Traffic Circles, sheet 1 of 4, Drawing No. S-524.0. Checked by Priv. Engr., Sr. T.E. JV, Pr. T.E. BS, drawn by Priv. Engr., T.E. MN.
notes:
NOTES:
1. This drawing shows options with both mountable and painted islands on the approaches; however, the actual design should use consistent treatments on each approach. Mountable islands are preferred; painted islands may be used when islands are less than 50 square feet (SF) in size. If raised center island is used, roundabout directional arrow signs (R6-4) should be included in the center island.
2. All signs and pavement markings shown in California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CA MUTCD), current edition shall be implemented as specified.
3. Signs shown for only one approach, but should be provided consistently on each approach.
4. For diameter dimensions of center island, see sheet 4 of 4.
5. Install new curb ramps and crosswalks as shown. Diagonal ramps may not be used. Existing ramps within the circulating lane must be removed.
6. Crosswalks may be supplemented with pedestrian activated rectangular rapid flashing beacons (RRFBs).
7. See City of Los Angeles Supplemental Street Design Guide Detail 710 for mini-roundabout details.

Callouts: Non-walkable area. 4" solid yellow edge line, 1' off mountable center island. Center island mountable or painted, see Note 1 and see sheet 2. Solid white edge line. Mountable splitter island. Solid white arrow symbols (optional for raised islands, required for painted islands). Dashed white entrance line, 12" wide, 2' long at 2' gap. Optional splitter island formed by two sets of double yellow lines, see Note 1 on sheet 2. 4" solid yellow edge line, 1' off mountable splitter island. Crosswalk markings, see Note 6. 20' (TYP). Red curb, see DOT Std Plan S-481.
title: Mini-Roundabouts
summary: First of four sheets. Dimensions on the lower approach are 100 ft, 200 ft and 32 ft. Seven notes cover consistent island treatments, MUTCD signs and markings, curb ramps, RRFBs and Supplemental Street Design Guide Detail 710. Approved 02-20-2020.

description:

Each approach has a painted splitter island outlined by double yellow lines, tapering from a thin double centerline on the outer end to a wide flared end at the circle. The detailed approach on the left shows the splitter island dimensioned: 15' DESIRABLE for the tapered section before the crosswalk, 10' (TYP) for the crosswalk zone, and 20' from the crosswalk to the entry end, with the island width at the entry dimensioned 11' - 14' ('WIDTH VARIES BY SITE CONDITIONS. SEE NOTE 3'). A crosswalk of transverse bars crosses the street at the splitter island, with a curb ramp (type varies) at each curb. Non-walkable areas are shown along the curb returns. Other approaches repeat the layout with crosswalks and double yellow lines.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Mini-Roundabouts and Neighborhood Traffic Circles, sheet 2 of 4, Drawing No. S-524.0.
notes:
NOTES:
1. Painted splitter islands may be used when site geometry leads to islands less than 50 SF in size.
2. Use dimension schedule on sheet 4 of 4 as a design guide. Final dimensions to be determined by the engineer.
3. Where crossing streets are not the same width, consider curb extensions on wider road to create consistent approach widths.
4. Type D pavement markers placed on the yellow centerline are required for painted center islands and splitter islands and recommended for raised splitter and center islands. Use 12 for less than or equal to 15' diameter (<= 15' DIA.). Use 16 for greater than 15' diameter and less than 20' diameter (> 15' DIA. < 20' DIA.). Use 20 for greater than or equal to 20' diameter (>= 20' DIA.).

description:

description:
Center island geometry, plan view: An intersection of two streets with rounded curb returns and a circular center island of diameter C. A dashed ring just outside the island marks the optional truck apron, and the island is labeled CENTER ISLAND. Dimension A is shown as the street width (between curb faces) on both the vertical and horizontal streets. Dimension B is the curb return radius, drawn as a radial dimension at the lower right curb return. The offset (5.5' MAX, see Note 3) is measured from the street edge line extension to the island. The opening width, between the island (or truck apron) and the curb return, varies 16'-20' (see Notes 3 and 4).

Opening width table (Table 1): offset to opening width, offset 5.5' (MAX) = 16' (MIN); 5.0 = 17'; 4.5 = 18'; 4.0 = 19'; 3.5 OR LESS = 20' (MAX).

Dimensions table (Table 2): street width A, curb return radius B, center island diameter C. A = 28' (Hillside Limited Standard): B 15', 20', 25' gives C 18', 20', 22'. A = 30' (Local Street Limited): B 15', 20', 25' gives C 20', 22', 24'. A = 36' (Local Street Standard): B 15', 20', 25' gives C 27', 29', 33'. A = 40' (Collector): B 15', 20', 25' gives C 32', 34', 38'.
